# Allocation baselines for the self-host compiler compiling one real module,
# checked against every run by scripts/ci-check-perf.
#
# FORMAT: metric  value  [tolerance%]. The metric key is
# <arch>/<subject>.<allocs|frees> — heap events the compiler performed while
# compiling examples/self_host/checker.fern against internal/stdlib, counted by
# a FERN_LEAKCHECK-instrumented build (scripts/selfhost-alloc-bench).
#
# EXACT FOR A GIVEN CHECKOUT PATH, and that qualifier is the whole subtlety
# here. These count events the program performed rather than time it took, so on
# one path they repeat to the digit over every run. But the compiler is handed
# ABSOLUTE paths to the subject and the stdlib, and it allocates a handful more
# for a longer one: measured on one binary, /home/user/lang gives 14520755,
# GitHub's /home/runner/work/lang/lang gives 14520754, and a deeply-nested path
# gives 14520750. That is four orders of magnitude inside the 1% tolerance, so it
# cannot trip the gate — but it does mean a local run legitimately differs from
# CI by a few counts, and that is not a regression to chase. The tolerance stays
# a significance threshold rather than a noise floor, the same as the
# instruction-count lanes.
#
# The figures banked below are the ones GitHub's runner produces, since that is
# where the gate runs; a local run reads a little high.
#
# WHY THE GAP. allocs exceeds frees by the ~3.03M objects live when the process
# exits — a compiler that runs once and exits does not tear its world down. The
# two are baselined separately so a change that stops freeing shows up as one
# row moving rather than being netted away.
#
# PEAK RSS IS DELIBERATELY ABSENT. scripts/selfhost-alloc-bench can also read
# peak RSS out of a scratch cgroup, and that figure is not comparable across
# hosts — transparent_hugepage alone spreads the same allocation 12x — so it
# cannot be baselined against whatever runner CI hands you. The lane sets
# FERN_ALLOC_PEAK_RSS=0; peak RSS stays a local instrument, worked through in
# docs/SELFHOST-SYMBOL-INTERNING.md.
#
# x86_64 ONLY, like the append-cliff lane: the aarch64 lane does not build a
# self-host compiler. Keys stay arch-namespaced anyway, so adding that arch
# later does not renumber this one.
#
# ADVISORY, IN BOTH DIRECTIONS — see scripts/ci-check-perf. When a number moves
# on purpose, update it in the same PR; the job summary prints the corrected
# lines ready to paste. Keep the reason in the PR, not here.

x86_64/checker.allocs	14520754
x86_64/checker.frees	11486354
